sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of Northwestern and Central Nigeria. Circulation draft, May 2012. 369 pp. (Wayback capture of rogerblench.info)
sources.note: sec.3.8.4 'Wəri-Gwamhyə-Mba' (pp.29-30) is sociolinguistic (autonyms, villages, vitality, wordlists taken 2010-11); the only prosodic remark is p.30 'The differences [between the three lects] are said to largely lie in the tonation.' sec.4.8.4 'Wuri cluster' under 4. Phonology (p.36) is an empty heading. Comparative wordlist appendix gives untoned Gwamhyə/Wurə/Gwamhɪ-R forms. No stress statement.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. In S. McGill & P. K. Austin (eds), Language Documentation and Description 11: 90-135. London: SOAS.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.121: 'Wuri and Gwamhy are two ethnic groups speaking dialects of a single language, completely undescribed apart from a few nouns in Rowlands (1962).' Sociolinguistic vitality report only (fieldwork 2011-12 at Bori near Maga).
